claude.sample_unit: simulated patients sampled from 133,262 synthetic patients

links.outcome: Proportion of simulated patients falling below k-anonymity thresholds under cumulative quasi-identifier disclosure after per-turn de-identification
links.effect: 79.9% (3,994; 95% CI 78.8-81.0%) reached k<5; 86.2% reached k<11; 64.6% uniquely identifiable (k=1); median 7 steps to k<5, 4 when rarest first.
links.quote: Of 5,000 randomly sampled patients, 79.9% (3,994; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 78.8% to 81.0%) reached k < 5 at some point during their disclosure sequence, while 86.2% (4,311; 95% CI: 85.2 to 87.2%) reached k < 11 .

links.outcome: Cumulative quasi-identifier disclosure across multi-turn LLM prompts eroding anonymity beyond the minimum necessary
links.effect: Even with no direct identifiers per turn, 79.9% of patients reached k<5 within a disclosure sequence; median 7 steps under progressive disclosure.
links.quote: The re-identification risk emerges not from any non-compliant disclosure but from the steady accumulation of compliant ones.

unlisted_practices: Real-time k-anonymity monitoring of clinician-LLM conversations (proposed, not tested)
On-premise open-source LLM deployment or BAA cloud services to reduce adversary pool (discussed, not tested)

links.effect: 79.9% reached k < 5; 64.6% reached k = 1 by end of sequence.
links.quote: Of the 5,000 sampled patients, 64.6% (3,228) were uniquely identifiable ( k = 1 ) within the synthetic reference population by the end of their disclosure sequence.
